analysis.title: Enterprise Products Partners LP (EPD): First Take: 3Q26 Beat; Solid Permian Volume Trend
key_insights: EPD reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $2,789m, above GSe of $2,654m (+5%) and FactSet consensus of $2,673m (+4%). Natural Gas and Petchem results largely offset lower Crude contributions.
Permian G&P volumes continued to beat GS expectations. EPD raised its long-term Permian macro outlook, implying higher gas-to-oil ratios (GORs), now closer to GSe.
Optimization gains declined sequentially, as GS expected, but remain a tailwind. GS calls it a relatively quiet quarter that is solid against recently mixed investor sentiment.

NGL segment operating margin was $1,535m, 1% above GSe of $1,516m. Processing margins were below expectations (better fee-based offset by lower POP) and down QoQ, offset by stronger marketing. NGL transport volumes were in line with GSe and +1% QoQ.
NGL export volumes were 11% above GSe but -2% QoQ. NGL frac volumes were largely in line and +2% QoQ, with modestly stronger fees than GSe.
Crude oil segment margin was $367m, 12% below GSe of $417m. Volumes were 8% below GSe and 11% lower QoQ. Sequential decline reflected lower optimization, higher costs and lower Seaway volumes.

Natural gas segment operating margin was $411m, 16% above GSe of $353m. Transportation volumes were 10% above GSe and +8% QoQ. Margin fell sequentially on lower marketing and optimization opportunities.

Petchems/products segment operating margin was $430m, 5% above GSe of $411m and +3% QoQ. Stronger octane volumes and refined products rates drove the beat, offsetting PDH downtime and lower ethylene exports.

Capex was $1,048m versus GSe of $923m and consensus of $995m. 2026 sustaining capex guidance rose to $650m from $600m. FY26 growth capex stays at $2.9-3.4b (excluding $600m asset sales guidance) and FY27 at ~$3b, versus GSe of $3.46b/$2.98b.
EPD kept its quarterly distribution at $0.56 and repurchased $112m of units versus GSe of $138m.

EPD raised its Permian production forecast since its April Fundamentals Outlook: +3.2 bcf/d of incremental wet gas growth to 38.6 bcf/d by 2030, supported by GOR strength. The NGL production forecast rose 0.5 mmb/d to a 5.2 mmb/d 2030 exit.

GS leaves its price target and estimates unchanged ahead of the call. Expected questions: normalizing optimization into 2027, Permian activity pace and GORs, Permian market share retention, and unitholder returns.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral with a 12-month target of $38 based on 10.25x 2027 EBITDA. Target and estimates are unchanged after the 3Q26 beat. The stock closed at $38.06 on 28 Oct, 0.2% above the target.

earnings_insights: EPD 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $2,789m vs GS estimate $2,654m and FactSet consensus est $2,673m (reported 10/29). 2Q26 reported: $2,829m.
3Q26 DCF reported $2,312m vs GS estimate $2,125m and consensus est $2,093m. Distribution $0.56 per unit, in line with GSe and consensus.
3Q26 capex reported $1,048m vs GS estimate $923m and consensus est $995m.
Segment margins reported 3Q26 vs GSe: NGL $1,535m vs $1,516m, Crude $367m vs $417m, Natural Gas $411m vs $353m, Petchem/refined products $430m vs $411m.
The call focus: run-rate base business performance, size of optimization upside, soft 2027 EBITDA commentary, long-term Permian production growth, and capital allocation.
risk_factors: Upside risks: stronger NGL and petchem prices, FID of large capital projects with better than expected returns, lower run-rate capex needs.
Downside risks: slower recovery in NGL and petchem demand, more competition in NGL pipeline, frac and export, and high-multiple acquisitions.
